title: connectors: `sys_connector_credential` + open-tier resolver chain (env → credential object → vault), reconcile on credential change, install-local prompt for missing `credentialRef`s (ruling A on #27230)
body:
**Filing gate ③** (maintainer ruling). Ruled on #27230, letter **A**, comment 6468327468, 2026-10-28; the maintainer's words in the session thread, verbatim: 「同意」, after the options were put to them directly (「不过具体的决策细节你现在直接和我沟通就行」). Sub-question S1 ruled there too: 「暂时不考虑 一个环境里住多个组织的情况，这种只有我们的云控制台在用，这种模式下可以不支持。」 This is the server half; the Console half is the sibling card filed in the same batch.

**Filed by** `session_01J8VVAjRKqdoEYQ4hXxtBuf`. ⛔ Not a claim. Lane suggestion: `domain:server` (`packages/services/service-automation`, `packages/cloud-connection`, possibly `packages/platform-objects` for the object's registration home per ADR-0029 D1 — the lane decides). Triage sets labels and priority; the decision card carried `priority:p2`.

**Business reason.** A declarative connector names its credential (`auth.credentialRef`) and the open tier resolves that name **only from `process.env`, once at boot** (`packages/services/service-automation/src/credential-resolver.ts`). The customer's administrator, who installs the app and holds the vendor key, has no server env on a hosted environment, so every connector-bearing app (HotCRM's Slack today; Stripe, GitHub, Google and the whole B wave of #26709 / #26702 / #26710) installs but cannot be credentialed. The metadata author and the administrator are two different people; this card gives the administrator a door and the runtime a chain.

**Who acts.** The `domain:server` seat; the `domain:ui` sibling consumes the REST surface this card exposes. Readers: administrators (through the sibling page), app authors (the docs section on `credentialRef` resolution), the install flow.

**Dedupe**: #27230's two searches (2026-10-28) — "connector credentialRef resolve settings secret store admin settings page …" → #24530 (closed, `sys_secret` / `sys_flow_credential` to deployment level — the seam this card reuses) and #7902 (closed); nothing open covers it.

### Governing text

- **ADR-0097 §3**: "`credentialRef` resolves through the secrets service at materialization time … static credentials resolved from env/config are **open**; managed vaulting, OAuth2 refresh, and per-tenant connection lifecycle are **enterprise**." A credential object is config; it stays open. Re-check: `git grep -n "resolved from env/config" origin/main -- docs/adr/0097-declarative-connector-instances.md`.
- **`sys_flow_credential` header** (`packages/services/service-automation/src/sys-flow-credential.object.ts`): the `Field.secret()` channel — "the engine encrypts it on write through the host's `ICryptoProvider` (fail-closed with no provider), masks it on every read path, and only the privileged `resolveSecretField()` dereferences it". Re-check: `git grep -n "resolveSecretField" origin/main -- packages/services/service-automation/src/flow-credential-channel.ts`.
- **ADR-0029 D1**: a capability plugin owns its `sys_*` objects alongside its behaviour.
- **AGENTS.md Prime Directive #9**: any new env var is `OS_{DOMAIN}_{FEATURE}`; this card should need none.
- **#27230 ruling comment 6468327468** (the authority for scope).

**Protocol statement.** `Metadata-protocol: none` for authors (the `credentialRef` key is unchanged). A new `sys_connector_credential` object and new REST routes under the automation domain; the route ledger and error-code ledger (ADR-0112) gain entries. `Skills-docs: follow-up owed — content/docs/automation/connectors.mdx` ("What `credentialRef` resolves through" currently says env only), plus an administrator page (where the sibling card lands the UI) and #27223's recipes (the author/administrator hand-off sentence).

### Premises (each with a re-check; read at `c3fb185a`)

1. Open-tier resolution is env-only and runs once at boot. Re-check: `git grep -n "defaultEnvCredentialResolver" origin/main -- packages/services/service-automation/src`.
2. The `Field.secret()` channel exists and is dereferenced by `resolveSecretField()`. Re-check: as above.
3. Hot reload reconciles instances by a signature of provider + config + auth (`metadata:reloaded`). Whether a **credential-row** change can fire that reconcile is **not measured** — first thing the dev verifies. Re-check: `git grep -n "metadata:reloaded" origin/main -- packages/services/service-automation/src/plugin.ts`.
4. Install-local registers the package and seeds data; whether it can read the package's declared `credentialRef`s before registration is **not measured**. Re-check: `git grep -n "connectors" origin/main -- packages/cloud-connection/src/marketplace-install-local-plugin.ts`.
5. Whether hosted runtimes ship the `openapi` / `mcp` / `rest` provider plugins by default is **not read**; if not, a credentialed connector still cannot boot there and that is a separate finding, not this card's scope.

### Work

1. **Object** `sys_connector_credential`: `ref` (the `credentialRef` text, unique per environment), `value` (`Field.secret()`), `connector_name` / `package_id` (derived from the declaring instances, informational), `status` (`set | missing | rejected`), `last_verified_at`, `updated_by`. Environment-level only (S1). Registration home per ADR-0029 D1 (the automation service, or platform-objects if the ledger-owner precedent applies — lane's call, stated in the PR).
2. **Resolver chain** in the open tier: env → `sys_connector_credential` (via `resolveSecretField()`) → the injected enterprise resolver if any. Env wins so a self-hosted operator keeps today's path; the object reports `source: env` for such a ref (read-only in the UI).
3. **Reconcile on change**: a write to a credential row re-materializes every instance whose `auth.credentialRef` names it, through the existing reconcile, without a restart. A rejected credential (upstream 401 at materialization) marks the row `rejected` with the connector's message, never the value.
4. **Declared-refs surface**: `GET /api/v1/automation/connectors/credential-refs` listing every `credentialRef` declared by installed packages with connector, package and status; `PUT /…/credential-refs/:ref` to set (write-only; never readable back), `DELETE` to clear; `manage_metadata`-gated. Route ledger and error codes registered.
5. **Install prompt** (server half): install-local answers, for the package being installed, the refs it declares and which are missing, so the sibling's dialog can ask; a skipped ref installs the package with that instance degraded, not refused.
6. **Docs**: the `credentialRef` resolution section of `content/docs/automation/connectors.mdx` rewritten for the chain; a changeset per touched package.

### Acceptance

- Fresh environment, no env vars, HotCRM installed with its Slack (or a test `openapi`) connector: the instance is `degraded` naming the missing ref; `PUT` the value; within the reconcile window the instance is ready and a flow `connector_action` dispatches; no restart.
- The value never appears in logs, in `GET /api/v1/automation/connectors`, in the audit (only "who changed which ref when"), or in any read of the object (masked).
- With `STRIPE_SECRET_KEY` set in env and a row present, env wins and the listing says `source: env`.
- A wrong value: instance `degraded`, row `rejected` with the upstream message, still no restart needed to fix.
- Walled postures (`group` / `isolated`): the routes refuse as every environment-metadata write does there (S1: not supported), with a message naming the posture.

### Out of scope

- The Console page and install dialog: the `domain:ui` sibling.
- App-shipped settings manifests (option B): its own card when HotCLM's provider selection needs it.
- OAuth connections and refresh: #26702. Request signing: #26710.
- Per-organization credentials on shared environments: ruled not supported.

### Related

#27230 (ruling) · #26702 · #26709 · #26710 · #27223 · #20790 (`sys_flow_credential`) · ADR-0097 · ADR-0007 · ADR-0029.
